source_note: yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave documents an unpacked DAVE.EXE claimed to be SHA1 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13, independently confirmed here (see EXT_SPECIMEN_IDENTITY) to be byte-identical to build/DAVE_unpacked.exe, so its addresses genuinely refer to the exact same bytes we have.
coordinate_convention_summary: Three distinct, unlabeled conventions found in the source, disentangled by cross-checking against our own disassembly (see tools/verify_external_re.py's module docstring for the full derivation): (1) explicit 'offset X from the file' phrasing / raw Python file slices -> literal file_offset, no conversion; (2) 'sub_XXXXX' IDA code addresses -> file_offset = coordinates.load_module_to_file_offset(sub_addr - 0x10000) [IDA assumed a code-segment linear base of 0x10000, i.e. paragraph 0x1000, rather than this program's real e_cs=0x0000]; (3) 'word_XXXXX' IDA data addresses -> literal DS-relative operand displacement, not converted (this project has not yet established the DS segment's own file-offset base).

facts.claimed_semantics: The external repo's own committed DAVE.EXE (already unpacked, 172848 bytes) is the same specimen as build/DAVE_unpacked.exe, SHA1 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13.
facts.verification_evidence: Downloaded the external repo's own DAVE.EXE via `gh api repos/yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave/contents/DAVE.EXE`, computed its SHA1 ourselves: 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13. This equals build/DAVE_unpacked.exe's own pinned SHA1 (layout/manifest.json / docs/specimen-manifest.json), and our own SHA1 of build/DAVE_unpacked.exe (computed in this same run) is 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13. Independent, not merely quoted from either party's README.

facts.claimed_semantics: The README states the ORIGINAL PACKED DAVE.EXE is 76597 bytes, SHA1 b0e70846c31d651b53c2f5490f516d8fd4844ed7.
facts.verification_evidence: Our own packed original (assets/DAVE.EXE, per docs/specimen-manifest.json) is 76586 bytes, SHA1 a8e14979d4259bc086b7d6b8ced575c66c4f9fef -- a DIFFERENT size and hash from the external project's stated packed file (76597 bytes / b0e70846c31d651b53c2f5490f516d8fd4844ed7). The two packed distributions differ (consistent with different LZEXE packing runs/releases of the same underlying program), but this does NOT affect the core premise: both UNPACK to the exact same 172848-byte image (see EXT_SPECIMEN_IDENTITY), which is the only specimen identity this project's addresses/facts depend on.

facts.verification_evidence: Disassembled build/DAVE_unpacked.exe at file offset 0x3d8b (inside census function F_3BA3, start 0x3ba3): the call targets found in order, ['0x769b', '0xdfb', '0xdfb', '0x4e69', '0x7831', '0x8eda', '0x4d9c', '0x3435'], exactly equal the claimed sub_XXXXX addresses converted via this fact's coordinate rule, ['0x769b', '0xdfb', '0xdfb', '0x4e69', '0x7831', '0x8eda', '0x4d9c', '0x3435']. facts.verification_evidence: Disassembled build/DAVE_unpacked.exe at file offset 0x3691 (inside census function F_34CB, start 0x34cb): found, in exact order, mov ax,[0x56f4]; mov [0x6152],ax (g_curr_warp_zone_mapping=g_current_level); bx=[0x56f4]*2; mov ax,[bx+0x192] (var2); bx=[0x56f4]*2; mov si,[bx+0x1a6] (var3); bx=[0x56f4]*2; mov ax,[bx+0x16a]; dec ax; mov [0x56f4],ax (g_current_level=table[0x16a][level]-1); call 0x4c69 (sub_14C69, converts to file offset 0x4e69 = census F_4E69); a few instructions later, mov word ptr [0x56ec], 0x10 (g_start_y=0x10). Every claimed detail matches byte-for-byte.

facts.source_address: 0x2583a (author-stated raw file offset, self-validated with a Python file slice)
facts.claimed_semantics: 10x uint16 LE table (indexed by 0-based level number) giving the level to warp back to +1, i.e. table[level]-1 == destination level; values (0,0,0,0,2,0,0,6,7,1) mean only 1-based levels 5,8,9,10 are warp zones (values 2,6,7,1).
facts.verification_evidence: struct.unpack('<10H', build/DAVE_unpacked.exe[0x2583a:0x2583a+20]) == (0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 6, 7, 1), exactly matching the claimed (0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 6, 7, 1). This table is also the one referenced via DS-relative displacement +0x16a in EXT_WARP_TRANSITION_FUNCTION's disassembly, per the author's own (unverified by us beyond this) claim that +0x16a maps to file offset 0x2583a; we did not independently re-derive that specific DS-segment-base arithmetic (would require solving the DS segment's own base, a separate open frontier), but the table's existence and exact values AT this raw file offset are independently confirmed.

facts.source_address: 0x2932b (author-stated raw file offset, self-validated with a Python file slice)
facts.claimed_semantics: Level 6's out-of-bounds warp zone reads tile data from this address (reached via a 16-bit-wrapped g_current_level==-1 (0xFFFF) index into g_levels), explaining the documented out-of-bounds-read bug/video.

facts.provenance: yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave (attributed by the author to the third-party shikadi.net modding wiki, NOT independently re-verified by the author himself with a raw byte check -- unlike EXT_WARP_TARGET_LEVEL_TABLE and EXT_LEVEL6_BUGGY_WARP_DATA above, which he did verify with Python slices)
facts.source_address: 0x26E0A ('we already know the tiles start at offset 0x26E0A')
facts.external_coordinate_convention: presented as a raw file_offset, but see contradiction below
facts.claimed_semantics: g_levels (the main 10-element level array) starts at file offset 0x26E0A, each element 0x500 (1280) bytes: 256 bytes path data + 1000 bytes tiles (100x10) + 24 bytes padding.
facts.verification_evidence: (1) Direct inspection: build/DAVE_unpacked.exe[0x26e0a:+32] = 00 2f 8d 2f 8d 2f 8d 2f 00 c5 ce d4 c5 d2 a0 c6 c9 cc c5 ce c1 cd c5 a0 a8 ac cf d0 d4 ae a0 c6, which (XORing the high-bit-set run with 0x80) decodes to text '././././.ENTER FILENAME (,OPT. F' -- clearly a string (looks like an 'ENTER FILENAME...' style prompt), not packed path/tile binary data. (2) Internal arithmetic inconsistency with the author's OWN separately-verified fact: per his own description, level 6's warp data (index -1, i.e. 0xFFFF) is reached via 'g_levels_base + ((-1 * 0x500) mod 0x10000)', which independently-confirmed EQUALS file offset 0x2932b (EXT_LEVEL6_BUGGY_WARP_DATA). If g_levels_base were really 0x26e0a, the two possible wrap interpretations give 0x2690a (no-wrap subtraction) or 0x3690a (full 16-bit-wrapped addition) -- NEITHER equals the confirmed 0x2932b, and (0x2932b - 0x26e0a) / 0x500 = 7.426 is not even an integer multiple of the element stride. The claimed base address is inconsistent with the author's own verified data point and should not be trusted; the true base of g_levels is not yet independently re-derived by this project.

facts.source_address: an initialization/scoring function ('Further mysteries' section); word_XXXX data addresses embedded in its own quoted pseudocode are implicit (g_score_lo/hi, g_next_goal_lo/hi, g_lives) -- resolved here via disassembly, not stated numerically by the author
facts.external_coordinate_convention: n/a for this fact's own text (no explicit numeric address given for this function; we located it independently via the shared global addresses already established in EXT_INIT_FUNCTION: g_score_lo=0x4c60, g_score_hi=0x4c62, g_next_goal_lo=0x6148, g_next_goal_hi=0x614a, g_lives=0x56ee)
facts.claimed_semantics: Extra-life award: if ((score_hi - next_goal_hi) != (score_lo < next_goal_lo) || (score_lo - next_goal_lo > 0x4e20)) { next_goal_lo = score_lo; if (lives < 3) { UpdateSprite(...); lives++; PlaySound(0xc); } } Score cap: if (score_hi != 0 && (score_hi > 1 || score_lo > 0x869f)) { score_lo = 0x869f; score_hi = 1; } (caps total score at 99999).
facts.verification_evidence: Disassembled build/DAVE_unpacked.exe at file offset 0xc63 (inside census function F_0C34, start 0xc34): found mov ax,[0x4c62]; mov dx,[0x4c60]; sub dx,[0x6148]; sbb ax,[0x614a]; or ax,ax; jb skip; jne take; cmp dx,0x4e20; jb skip -- the exact 32-bit subtract-with-borrow encoding of the claimed OR condition -- followed by 'mov [0x6148],[0x4c60 via dx]; mov [0x614a],ax' (next_goal_lo=score_lo), 'cmp [0x56ee],3; jge skip2' (lives<3), an UpdateSprite-shaped call, 'inc [0x56ee]' (lives++), and 'call 0x743e' with arg 0xc (PlaySound(0xc)). Further down: 'cmp [0x4c62],1; jb skip3; ja clamp; cmp [0x4c60],0x869f; jbe skip3; clamp: mov [0x4c60],0x869f; mov [0x4c62],1' -- exactly the claimed score cap. Every constant (0x4e20, 0x869f, 1, 3) and every address matches.

facts.source_address: n/a (structural/format claim, not a single address)
facts.claimed_semantics: 10 normal levels, 100x10 tiles each, stored as 1280-byte records (256 bytes monster-path data + 1000 bytes tile IDs + 24 bytes padding), plus one special 10x7 tiles-only 'opening screen' level and a separate 10-element per-level start-position/motion array.
facts.verification_evidence: This structural claim's only anchor point given (g_levels at file offset 0x26E0A) is independently contradicted (see EXT_LEVELS_BASE_ADDRESS); without a confirmed base address we have no location to test the claimed 1280-byte/256+1000+24 record shape against. Re-deriving the correct base (e.g. by locating the real DS segment base, or by pattern-matching plausible tile-ID byte ranges) is left as future work, not attempted here to keep this pass's claims each independently falsifiable.
